claim_text: Charleston County Government says it identified a "sophisticated cyberattack" on its systems on Monday, Nov 16, 2026
summary: The county's Nov 19 release says it "continues to investigate a sophisticated cyberattack identified on Monday, November 16, 2026." Its Nov 17 release first called it a "potential cybersecurity incident."
detail: This is the county's own wording on its website, repeated by WCSC, WCBD, WCIV and South Carolina Public Radio. The county has not said how the attackers got in or who they are.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: A Tier 1 source, the county's own news release, calls it a cyberattack, and several independent outlets report the same statement.
notes: The county moved from "potential cybersecurity incident" (Nov 17) to "sophisticated cyberattack" (Nov 19).

claim_text: The county says its IT team noticed unusual network activity the evening of Nov 16, worked through the night to secure affected systems, and notified SLED that night
summary: The Nov 17 release says county IT identified unusual activity on its network on the evening of Monday, Nov 16, secured affected systems overnight, and that the South Carolina Law Enforcement Division (SLED) was notified and is on-site.
detail: The county has not said how long the unusual activity went on before it was noticed.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The county's own release (Tier 1), reported by WCSC and The Post and Courier.

claim_text: Data was copied (removed) from Charleston County systems
summary: The county says it has "confirmed that data was copied from its systems." Its Nov 17 release used the words "removed from its systems."
detail: The county has not said what data, how much, or from which systems. "Copied" and "removed" are the county's two wordings of the same finding.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The county's own releases (Tier 1) say it, and independent outlets report it.
notes: Confirmed that the county says so. What was in the data is not established (c006).

claim_text: SLED is treating the incident as a criminal investigation, with other state and federal agencies assisting
summary: The county's Nov 19 release says SLED's cybersecurity program is on-site assisting with the analysis "alongside other state and federal agencies" and that SLED "is now treating the incident as a criminal investigation."
detail: The release does not name the federal agencies. South Carolina Public Radio, WCBD and WCIV report the same.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The county's own release (Tier 1) says it, and independent outlets report it. SLED itself confirmed to WCIV on Nov 18 that its assistance began Tuesday, Nov 17, and was ongoing.
notes: SLED's confirmation to WCIV covers its assistance, not the criminal-investigation status, which rests on the county's Nov 19 release. SLED declined an interview and sent other questions to the county (WCIV). The Post and Courier reported on Nov 18 that SLED had not responded to its request for comment.

claim_text: Charleston County says day-to-day operations are unaffected and core life safety services remain intact
summary: The Nov 19 release says day-to-day county operations "remain unaffected" and core life safety services "remain intact and fully functional." The Nov 17 release said services to residents would continue as normal.
detail: This rests on the county's own statement, which the news outlets repeat. We found no report of a service disruption.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The county's own releases (Tier 1) say it, and independent outlets report it.
notes: Confirmed that the county says this. We did not check county services ourselves.

claim_text: What data was copied, and whether any personal or financial information was involved, is not established
summary: The county says investigators are "still working to determine the nature and extent of that data, including whether any personal or financial information was compromised."
detail: The county has not said what kind of data or how many people. No outlet reports a count. WCIV reports, citing the South Carolina Department of Consumer Affairs, that state law requires notices to affected residents when certain personal information is compromised, and a report to that department when more than 1,000 South Carolina residents are affected; no such notice for the county has been reported.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: The county's own releases (Tier 1) say the review is ongoing; no source says what was in the data.
notes: This and the root cause (c008) must be answered before the story can close.

claim_text: Who is behind the Charleston County cyberattack is not established
summary: Neither the county nor SLED has named an attacker. We found no outlet reporting an attribution.
detail: The county calls the attack "sophisticated" but gives no detail about the attacker.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: No official or independent source names an actor.
notes: Attribution stays Not established unless the county, SLED or independent forensic work names one.

claim_text: How the attackers got into the county's systems is not established
summary: The county's releases say unusual activity was found and data was copied. They do not say how access was gained.
detail: This is the root cause. Nothing in the sources we read describes the method, the systems involved or the weakness used.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: The county has not said, and no outlet reports a method.
notes: This must be answered before the story can close.

claim_text: Whether a ransomware group has claimed the attack, or any ransom demand was made or data published, is not established
summary: The county says nothing about a ransom, and no outlet reports a claim. One security newsletter's Nov 19 brief says no ransomware group has claimed it.
detail: We looked only at news coverage and did not visit any leak site, dark-web page or tracker. Absence of a claim in coverage is not proof none exists.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: No official or independent source reports a claim or a demand; the newsletter is one Tier 3 source.
notes: The newsletter's statement is a negative report, so it is context, not a finding.

claim_text: The Charleston County incident is part of the November 2026 wave of outages and disruptions
summary: The Post and Courier says the county incident came "amid" a nationwide run of outages, and reports that federal officials said they had no reason to believe those outages were connected to each other or malicious.
detail: The Post and Courier places the events in the same week; it does not link them. No source ties the county's attack to the outages or to any other incident.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: No source shows a connection; timing alone is not evidence.
notes: Separate from the county finding. Other isitahack pages cover those outages.
